edtech-product-managers-lms-audit-does-p.headline: EdTech Product Managers - LMS Audit - Does Product Manage Learning
edtech-product-managers-lms-audit-does-p.body:
The most successful education technology of the last twenty-five years has never taught anyone anything.\
It enrols students, files their PDFs, records attendance and posts grades. We call it a learning management system. Learning is the one thing it does not manage.\
For twenty-five articles I have prosecuted the university — the Factory of Facts, its assembly line of credits and semesters. This week I turn to the factory's suppliers, and open a new arc of ten: The EdTech Audit.\
The first finding is uncomfortable. An industry that raised billions promising to disrupt the factory went into business selling it faster conveyor belts.\
The evidence is in the logs. A full semester of LMS usage data at one large university: Announcements in 82% of courses. Grades in 71%. The discussion board — the one tool built for students to think in front of each other — in 21%.\
A noticeboard, a filing cabinet, and a ledger. The pedagogy in the basement.\
Why? Follow the invoice. The learner has never signed the cheque for an LMS. The registrar does. And a product serves whoever pays for it, with a fidelity no mission statement can override. I call it The Vendor Trap.\
Three questions I would ask of every EdTech product before a rupee moves: Does it touch the learning or the ledger? Whose week actually improves? What does it measure?\
The factory is closing. Its best supplier has not noticed.\
Full piece below — and I would genuinely like to hear from those of you inside EdTech: which of your products would pass all three questions? 👇#ReimagineEducation #EdTech #HigherEducation #LMS #EdTechAudit #AcademicLeadership #DigitalTransformation #LearningDesign #UniversityStrategy #NEP2020 #FutureOfEducation #EdTechIndia

business-and-technology-leaders-tech-bud.body:
Open call for experts: Where Are Business Leaders Focusing Their Tech Budgets As Tech Stock Market Volatility Persists\
\
This report is for Forbes. Open call to all experts to participate. Thanks! See details and link below. \
\
AI and tech stocks continue on a volatile trajectory, with Goldman Sachs reporting that hedge funds are selling US tech stocks at a record pace, and Bloomberg reporting that big tech needs to justify AI spending. \
\
Meanwhile, small, medium, and large business leaders, decision-makers, and executives, who are modernizing their tech and operations, are left to figure out the road ahead. \
\
Amid this volatility, a new report from Forrester Research agrees that tech leaders face “sustained pressure to deliver value, modernize for AI, govern at speed, and maintain trust — all amid persistent volatility and budget scrutiny”.\
\
However, the same report found that more than 80% of business and technology leaders expect budget increases for 2027, highlighting strategic areas of investment for next year. \
\
For this report, I am looking for expert sources to provide clear signals for small, medium, and large business owners and decision-makers to help them navigate the current landscape and plan for 2027. \
\
